title: 6/07–6/10 fetch-contest-streak sent a daily false 'failed' DM on the expected morning settlement lag
tier_reason: recurring false failure DM (alert noise; throttled to at most one per 6 h); the gate still refused to overwrite, so contest state and picks were unaffected

contract.text: fetch-contest-streak refuses to overwrite with a non-advancing observation but alerts only on genuine staleness (two or more settled picks behind); the normal one-settled-pick morning lag exits quietly with no DM.
contract.source: 8cd7207 (src/bts/cli.py fetch_contest_streak step 4, 'mirrors the level-aware health check'); tests/test_cli_integration.py::TestFetchContestStreak::test_expected_settlement_lag_no_write_no_alert

mechanism.text: the currentness gate in fetch_contest_streak called _fail (throttled 'BTS fetch-contest-streak failed' DM + exit 2) whenever the profile's source_date was earlier than the latest resolved local pick, which is the normal morning state because the contest settles day D the next day; the 01:10/02:10/10:30/13:30 ET cron (with --dm-recipient) ran it into that state daily

watchdog.trigger: a fetch-contest-streak failure DM (or nonzero exit in cron.log) whose reason is 'not current' while the profile trails local settlement by exactly one settled pick — the expected morning state reported as a failure
watchdog.recovery_assertion: by the 13:30 ET fetch the observation advances to the latest settled pick and is written; a one-step lag produces exit 0 and no DM, while a lag of two or more settled picks still alerts

evidence.what: the currentness gate DM'd on every fetch where the profile lagged the latest pick — the normal morning state — 'so it fired a "failed" DM daily'

evidence.locator: commit 8cd7207^ (279d423) src/bts/cli.py fetch_contest_streak and _contest_fetch_alert; commit 68a35d3 diff (scripts/cron-setup-hetzner.sh)
evidence.what: the lag branch called _fail, which sends 'BTS fetch-contest-streak failed: …' (6 h cooldown) and exits 2; the cron runs it at 01:10, 02:10, 10:30 and 13:30 ET with --dm-recipient, logging to cron.log
